skill.name: webask-lead-quality
skill.description: Analyzes WebAsk survey leads by contact completion, apparent contact quality, contact-stage losses, and acquisition channel.
skill.summary: Assess usable contact rates and identify where WebAsk surveys lose potential leads.
skill.author: webaskio

content.value_statement: Survey completion counts can hide missing or unusable contact details. This skill guides assistants through WebAsk reports to assess contact quality, compare channels, and prioritize improvements.
actual_capabilities: Identify phone, email, and name questions through the survey structure tool.
Calculate contact submission rates relative to all survey starters using available report data.
Compare responses before the contact question with responses to the contact question to estimate losses.
Separate obviously suspicious contact values from apparently usable contacts using simple heuristics.
Compare lead quality across acquisition channels when source labels are available.
Present aggregate metrics and prioritize recommendations about contact timing, required fields, and explanatory text.
limitations: Requires access to the four declared WebAsk MCP tools and relevant survey data; tool implementations are not included.
Contact quality checks are heuristic and do not verify phone reachability, email ownership, or sales qualification.
Channel comparisons require source labels, and cost comparisons require spending data that the skill does not explicitly retrieve.
Provides analysis and recommendations, not automatic survey edits, CRM synchronization, or contact exports.

use_cases.title: Compare Acquisition Channels
use_cases.description: Compare apparently usable contact rates across labeled sources to identify channels that generate stronger leads.

use_cases.title: Assess Sales Intake Quality
use_cases.description: Separate survey completions from submissions with apparently usable contacts before evaluating the incoming lead volume.

use_cases.title: Review Contact Collection
use_cases.description: Identify losses around contact questions and prioritize changes to field requirements, question order, and contact explanations.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Lead Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze WebAsk survey [survey]. Show starters, contact submissions, apparently usable contacts, and their share of starters. Keep personal contact details out of chat.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: obtain a basic lead quality summary.

prompt_templates.title: Locate Contact Losses
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [survey] and compare response counts before and at the contact question. Estimate the loss and suggest prioritized improvements. State data limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: investigate a weak contact conversion rate.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Source Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare lead quality for each source label in [survey]. Show counts and usable contact rates. Identify missing labels and avoid unsupported cost claims.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Prioritized Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [survey] across contact conversion, suspicious values, and labeled channels. Explain denominators and heuristic limits. Rank recommendations by expected impact without changing the survey.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine funnel analysis with a prioritized improvement review.

output_examples.input: Illustrative data: 512 starters, 243 reached the contact step, 186 submitted contacts, and 164 contacts appear usable. Summarize lead quality.
output: Started: 512. Reached contact: 243. Submitted contact: 186. Apparently usable contacts: 164.
Contact submission rate: 36.3% of starters. Apparently usable contact rate: 32.0% of starters.
Contact-stage gap: 57 participants. Suspicious contact submissions: 22.
Review the contact explanation and unnecessary fields. These counts do not establish why participants stopped.

output_examples.input: Illustrative labeled data: newsletter has 100 starters and 38 usable contacts; website banner has 100 starters and 19. Compare these sources.
output: Newsletter: 38 apparently usable contacts from 100 starters, or 38%.
Website banner: 19 apparently usable contacts from 100 starters, or 19%.
Newsletter has the higher observed usable contact rate. Costs and eventual sales outcomes are unavailable.
Review banner traffic expectations and contact questions before making budget decisions.

best_practices: Use all survey starters as the denominator and distinguish submitted contacts from apparently usable contacts.
Keep personal contact details out of chat and report aggregate counts.
Check source labels, report completeness, and heuristic assumptions before prioritizing changes.
anti_patterns: Treating every completed survey as a qualified lead, even when contact details are missing.
Assuming suspicious contact formats prove that a person is unreachable or unqualified.
Removing every required field or claiming channel cost advantages without spending data.

faq.question: What does this skill measure?
faq.answer: It focuses on contact submissions, apparently usable contacts, losses around contact questions, and differences between labeled acquisition channels.

faq.question: Which tools does it require?
faq.answer: It declares get_quiz_structure, get_quiz_summary, get_quiz_report, and get_answer_extra_field_values as WebAsk MCP dependencies.

faq.question: Does it verify phone numbers or email addresses?
faq.answer: No. It flags obviously suspicious values through heuristics, without confirming reachability, ownership, or sales readiness.

faq.question: Can it compare acquisition channels?
faq.answer: Yes, when source labels and suitable report data exist. Comparing costs also requires spending data.

faq.question: Will it show personal contacts or update my CRM?
faq.answer: The instructions prohibit posting contacts in chat. The supplied skill does not provide a CRM update or export workflow.

faq.question: What happens when a service limit prevents analysis?
faq.answer: The instructions require the assistant to state the limit and stop, without recommending an upgrade or directing users to payment.
